thought.text: I'll install Node.js 22 LTS (needed for Vite 8) from the official tarball.

reasoning_content:
Ubuntu 22.04. Vite 8 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ (actually does Vite 8 require Node 20.19+ or 22.12+? Let me check: Vite 7 requires Node 20.19+ / 22.12+. Vite 8 probably requires Node 20.19+ or 22.12+ too). Also, does React 19 require Node 20+? Node 18 ships with Ubuntu 22.04, but for this project Node 20 or 22 is probably required.

I'll install Node.js 22 via NodeSource (the standard method). I'll use the nodesource setup script. This is the "curl | bash" pattern, which is somewhat risky, but NodeSource is the official channel. Alternatively, I could download the tarball directly from nodejs.org. Let me download the Node 22 LTS tarball directly — that's cleaner and doesn't involve piping to shell.

I'll go with downloading the official Node.js tarball from nodejs.org.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /tmp && curl -fsSL -o node.tar.xz https://nodejs.org/dist/v22.20.0/node-v22.20.0-linux-x64.tar.xz && ls -la node.tar.xz", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Download Node.js 22 tarball from nodejs.org"}
